geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the dominant bar but author a clearer sectional/profiled massing rule instead of a generic slab.
Increase the bend enough to make the longitudinal curve visible in all views and strengthen silhouette continuity.
Refine the bend so the curved profile reads as one continuous mass rather than a stepped extrusion.
Align the courtyard opening to the verified access edge to create a legible public threshold.
Expand the carved court so the void becomes programmatic and public rather than decorative.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen form continuity and reduce the generic rectangular bar reading by making the primary mass more explicitly profiled.
Preserve the dominant longitudinal gesture while allowing the bend to express a clearer sectional profile.
Align the main subtraction toward the verified access side to improve public threshold legibility.
Enlarge the carved void so it reads as a usable public cut rather than a minor bite.
Increase void depth to make the ground response more legible and spatially consequential.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant bent-and-cantilevered bar with reasonable coherence across views, so gesture clarity and hierarchy are decent. The section is spatially legible, but the form remains fairly boxy and the carved/public void is too weak for the neighborhood-living brief. The thick blue access edge is not answered strongly enough: the ground condition appears mostly sealed, with only a modest notch/cut, so the public threshold is underdeveloped. The mass is not visibly self-colliding, and repair integrity is strong. However, program fit fails the hard gate because the visible mass does not convincingly establish the required active street edge plus one clear public void/terrace in a way that reads as a neighborhood commercial/mixed-use building; the open-space figure is incidental rather than dominant. The stepped upper treatment is coherent enough to avoid penalizing as arbitrary staircase mass, but it is not yet program-meaningful.
